The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

To compute the unadjusted EBITDA Margin for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to calculate EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) first. The formula is:

\[ \text{EBITDA} = \text{Operating Income} + \text{Interest Expense} - \text{Interest Income} + \text{Depreciation and Amortization} \]

From the provided financial statements:
- Operating income for 2024: $9,285 million
- Interest expense for 2024: $(169) million
- Interest income for 2024: $624 million
- Depreciation and amortization for 2024: $2,237 million

First, we calculate EBITDA:
\[ \text{EBITDA} = \$9,285 + (-\$169) - \$624 + \$2,237 = \$10,739 \text{ million} \]

Next, to find the unadjusted EBITDA Margin, we divide EBITDA by Total Revenue:
\[ \text{EBITDA Margin} = \frac{\text{EBITDA}}{\text{Total Revenue}} \]
\[ \text{EBITDA Margin} = \frac{10,739}{254,453} \times 100\% \approx 4.22\% \]

Therefore, the unadjusted EBITDA margin for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **4.22%**.

To determine if the Operating Profit Margin is greater in 2024 compared to 2023 for Costco Wholesale Corporation, we need to calculate the Operating Profit Margin for both years.

The formula for Operating Profit Margin is:
\[ \text{Operating Profit Margin} = \left( \frac{\text{Operating Income}}{\text{Total Revenue}} \right) \times 100 \]

**For 2024:**
- Total Revenue: $254,453 million
- Operating Income: $9,285 million

\[ \text{Operating Profit Margin (2024)} = \left( \frac{9,285}{254,453} \right) \times 100 = 3.65\% \]

**For 2023:**
- Total Revenue: $242,290 million
- Operating Income: $8,114 million

\[ \text{Operating Profit Margin (2023)} = \left( \frac{8,114}{242,290} \right) \times 100 = 3.35\% \]

Comparing the two results:
- Operating Profit Margin for 2024: 3.65%
- Operating Profit Margin for 2023: 3.35%

Therefore, the Operating Profit Margin is greater in 2024 compared to 2023.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

   \[
   \text{P/E Ratio} = \frac{\text{Stock Price}}{\text{Diluted EPS}}
   \]

   Plugging in the values:
   
   \[
   \text{P/E Ratio} = \frac{940}{16.56} \approx 57
   \]

Therefore, the P/E ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, using diluted EPS is approximately **57**.

To calculate the diluted EPS for Costco for the fiscal year ending September 1, 2024, we need to determine the fully diluted shares outstanding. Diluted EPS is calculated using the net income attributable to Costco and the total number of shares that would be outstanding if all dilutive securities (like stock options, RSUs) were exercised or converted.

### Given Data:
- Net income attributable to Costco: $7,367 million
- Basic shares outstanding: 443,914,000 shares
- Diluted shares outstanding: 444,759,000 shares (already provided in the context)

### Step-by-step Calculation:
1. **Identify Net Income Attributable to Costco**:
   - From the income statement: $7,367 million

2. **Use Fully Diluted Shares Outstanding**:
   - Provided in the context as 444,759,000 shares.

3. **Calculate Diluted EPS**:
\[ \text{Diluted EPS} = \frac{\text{Net Income Attributable to Costco}}{\text{Fully Diluted Shares Outstanding}} \]

Substitute the values:

\[ \text{Diluted EPS} = \frac{7,367}{444,759,000} \approx 16.56 \text{ per share} \]

This matches the diluted EPS provided in the context (Diluted EPS of $16.56).

### Conclusion:
The Diluted EPS for Costco for the fiscal year ending September 1, 2024 is **$16.56**.

To compute the Market Value of Equity (MVE) for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, we need to follow these steps:

### Step 1: Calculate Fully Diluted Shares Outstanding

**Fully diluted shares outstanding** includes all common stock that would be issued if all convertible securities and potential issuances were converted or exercised. This typically includes:

- Basic shares outstanding
- Additional shares from options and RSUs (Restricted Stock Units)
- Other dilutive securities like warrants, preferred stock, etc.

From the provided data:
- **Basic Shares Outstanding:** 443,914,000 as of September 1, 2024.
- **Diluted Shares Outstanding:** 444,759,000 as of September 1, 2024.

The diluted shares outstanding already include the impact of RSUs and other dilutive securities. Therefore, we will use the diluted share count for our MVE calculation:
\[ \text{Fully Diluted Shares Outstanding} = 444,759,000 \]

### Step 2: Calculate Market Value of Equity (MVE)

The **Market Value of Equity** is calculated by multiplying the fully diluted shares outstanding by the stock price.

- **Stock Price as of September 1, 2024:** $940 per share

\[ \text{Market Value of Equity} = \text{Fully Diluted Shares Outstanding} \times \text{Stock Price} \]

Plugging in the values:

\[ \text{MVE} = 444,759,000 \times 940 \]
\[ \text{MVE} = 418,680,260,000 \]

### Final Answer

The **Market Value of Equity** for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024 is:
\[ \$418.68\text{ billion} \]

To estimate the Cost of Equity using the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of 2024, we use the following formula:

\[ \text{Cost of Equity} = R_f + \beta (R_m - R_f) \]

Where:
- \( R_f \) is the risk-free rate.
- \( \beta \) is the beta coefficient for Costco Wholesale Corporation.
- \( R_m \) is the expected market return.

### Given Data
1. **Risk-Free Rate (\( R_f \))**: 4.617% (10-year Treasury yield as a proxy).
2. **Market Return (\( R_m \))**: 11%
3. **Beta (\( \beta \))**: 0.79

### Calculation
First, calculate the market risk premium:

\[ R_m - R_f = 11\% - 4.617\% = 6.383\% \]

Next, apply CAPM to find the cost of equity for Costco Wholesale Corporation:

\[ \text{Cost of Equity} = 4.617\% + (0.79 \times 6.383\%) \]
\[ \text{Cost of Equity} = 4.617\% + 5.029\% \]
\[ \text{Cost of Equity} = 9.646\% \]

### Conclusion
The estimated cost of equity for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **9.65%** using the CAPM model with the provided inputs and data context.

The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

From the "Note 8—Taxes" section:
- **Deferred tax assets** as of September 3, 2023: $2,107 million.
- **Deferred tax liabilities** as of September 3, 2023: $(1,989) million.

The net deferred tax asset (Operating Deferred Tax Asset) is calculated by subtracting the deferred tax liabilities from the deferred tax assets:

\[ \text{Net Deferred Tax Asset} = \$2,107 - (-\$1,989) = \$4,096 \]

Therefore, the Operating Deferred Tax Asset, net of deferred tax liabilities in 2023 is **$4,096 million**.

The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within

To calculate the excess cash for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Identify Operating Cash:**
   - The operating cash is calculated as the minimum between taking 2% of revenue and actual cash available.

2. **Revenue Calculation:**
   - Total Revenue = $254,453 million (as given in the income statement).

3. **Calculate 2% of Revenue:**
   \[
   0.02 \times 254,453 = 5,089.06 \text{ million dollars}
   \]

4. **Actual Cash Available at End of Year:**
   - Cash and cash equivalents = $9,906 million (as given in the balance sheet).

5. **Determine Operating Cash:**
   - Operating cash is the minimum between 2% of revenue ($5,089.06 million) and actual cash available ($9,906 million).
   \[
   \text{Operating Cash} = \min(5,089.06, 9,906) = 5,089.06 \text{ million dollars}
   \]

6. **Calculate Excess Cash:**
   - Excess cash is the actual cash available minus operating cash.
   \[
   \text{Excess Cash} = 9,906 - 5,089.06 = 4,816.94 \text{ million dollars}
   \]

Therefore, the excess cash in 2024 is **$4,816.94 million**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

To calculate ARPU (Average Revenue Per User) for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024:

1. **Total revenue** from the income statement is $254,453 million.

2. **Total paid members** include both Gold Star and Business memberships including affiliates as of September 1, 2024:
   - Gold Star: 63,700
   - Business (including affiliates): 12,500

   Total paid members = 63,700 + 12,500 = **76,200** thousand members.

3. Convert total paid members to a single unit:
   - 76,200 thousand members = 76,200,000 members

4. Calculate ARPU by dividing total revenue by the number of users (members):
   
   \[
   \text{ARPU} = \frac{\text{Total Revenue}}{\text{Number of Members}}
   \]

   \[
   \text{ARPU} = \frac{254,453}{76,200,000}
   \]

5. Calculate the result:

\[
\text{ARPU} = \frac{254,453}{76,200,000} \approx 3.34
\]

**Therefore, ARPU for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately $3.34 per member.**

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

To calculate the change in operating working capital from 2023 to 2024 for Costco Wholesale Corporation, we need to look at changes in current assets (excluding cash and short-term investments) and current liabilities. The relevant figures are:

### Current Assets:
- **Receivables**: Increased from $2,285 million in 2023 to $2,721 million in 2024.
- **Merchandise inventories**: Increased from $16,651 million in 2023 to $18,647 million in 2024.
- **Other current assets**: Slightly increased from $1,709 million in 2023 to $1,734 million in 2024.

### Current Liabilities:
- **Accounts payable**: Increased from $17,483 million in 2023 to $19,421 million in 2024.
- **Accrued salaries and benefits**: Increased from $4,278 million in 2023 to $4,794 million in 2024.
- **Deferred membership fees**: Increased from $2,337 million in 2023 to $2,501 million in 2024.
- **Current portion of long-term debt**: Decreased from $1,081 million in 2023 to $103 million in 2024.
- **Other current liabilities**: Relatively stable at $6,254 million in 2023 and $6,210 million in 2024.

### Calculating Changes:
**Change in Current Assets:**
\[ \text{Receivables} = (2721 - 2285) = 436 \]
\[ \text{Merchandise inventories} = (18,647 - 16,651) = 1996 \]
\[ \text{Other current assets} = (1734 - 1709) = 25 \]

Total increase in current assets:
\[ 436 + 1996 + 25 = 2457 \text{ million dollars} \]

**Change in Current Liabilities:**
\[ \text{Accounts payable} = (19,421 - 17,483) = 1938 \]
\[ \text{Accrued salaries and benefits} = (4,794 - 4,278) = 516 \]
\[ \text{Deferred membership fees} = (2,501 - 2,337) = 164 \]
\[ \text{Current portion of long-term debt} = (103 - 1,081) = -978 \]
\[ \text{Other current liabilities} = (6,210 - 6,254) = -44 \]

Total increase in current liabilities:
\[ 1938 + 516 + 164 - 978 - 44 = 1606 \text{ million dollars} \]

**Change in Operating Working Capital:**
\[ \Delta \text{Working Capital} = (2457) - (1606) = 851 \text{ million dollars} \]

### Considering the constraint of 2% of Revenue as max potential operating cash:
- **Revenue for 2023**: $242,290 million
- **Potential Operating Cash (2% of revenue)**: \( 2\% \times 242,290 = 4845.8 \text{ million dollars} \)

Since the actual change in operating working capital ($851 million) is well below this threshold, there's no need to adjust for the potential cash constraint.

Therefore, the **change in operating working capital from 2023 to 2024** is **$851 million**.

To calculate the Accounts Receivables Days for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to use the following formula:

\[ \text{Accounts Receivable Days} = \frac{\text{Average Accounts Receivable}}{\text{Net Credit Sales per Day}} \]

Where:
- **Average Accounts Receivable** is calculated as (Receivables at end of 2024 + Receivables at end of 2023) / 2
- **Net Credit Sales per Day** = Net Sales / Number of Days in the Year

### Step-by-Step Calculation:

1. **Average Accounts Receivable:**
   \[
   \text{Average Accounts Receivable} = \frac{\text{Receivables at end of 2024} + \text{Receivables at end of 2023}}{2}
   \]
   - Receivables, net at the end of 2024: $2,721 million
   - Receivables, net at the end of 2023: $2,285 million

   \[
   \text{Average Accounts Receivable} = \frac{2,721 + 2,285}{2} = \frac{5,006}{2} = 2,503 \text{ million dollars}
   \]

2. **Net Credit Sales per Day:**
   - Net sales for the year ending September 1, 2024: $249,625 million
   - Number of days in the fiscal year (52 weeks): 365 days

   \[
   \text{Net Credit Sales per Day} = \frac{\text{Net Sales}}{\text{Number of Days in Year}}
   \]

   \[
   \text{Net Credit Sales per Day} = \frac{249,625}{365} \approx 683.85 \text{ million dollars/day}
   \]

3. **Accounts Receivable Days:**
   
   \[
   \text{Accounts Receivable Days} = \frac{\text{Average Accounts Receivable}}{\text{Net Credit Sales per Day}}
   \]
   
   \[
   \text{Accounts Receivable Days} = \frac{2,503}{683.85} \approx 3.66 \text{ days}
   \]

### Conclusion:
The Accounts Receivables Days for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **3.66 days**.

To calculate the Inventory Turnover for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024, we need to use the formula:

\[ \text{Inventory Turnover} = \frac{\text{Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)}}{\text{Average Inventory}} \]

### Step 1: Identify Cost of Goods Sold (Merchandise Costs)
From the Income Statement:
- Merchandise costs for 2024 are $222,358 million.

### Step 2: Calculate Average Inventory
To find the average inventory, we need to calculate the inventory at the beginning and end of the year:

\[ \text{Average Inventory} = \frac{\text{Beginning Inventory + Ending Inventory}}{2} \]

From the Balance Sheet:
- Merchandise inventories for September 1, 2024 (ending) is $18,647 million.
- Merchandise inventories for September 3, 2023 (beginning) is $16,651 million.

So,

\[ \text{Average Inventory} = \frac{18,647 + 16,651}{2} = \frac{35,298}{2} = 17,649 \]

### Step 3: Calculate Inventory Turnover
Using the values calculated:

\[ \text{Inventory Turnover} = \frac{\text{Cost of Goods Sold}}{\text{Average Inventory}} \]
\[ \text{Inventory Turnover} = \frac{222,358}{17,649} \approx 12.59 \]

Thus, the Inventory Turnover for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **12.59**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as

reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This

approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies

Net sales increased $11,915 or 5% during 2024. The improvement was attributable to an increase in comparable sales and sales at new

the impact of one less week of sales in 2024. Lower gasoline prices negatively impacted net sales by $917, or 39 basis points, compared to
2023, with a 3% decrease in the average price per gallon. Changes in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar negatively impacted net sales
by approximately $474, 20 basis points, compared to 2023, attributable to our Canadian and Other International operations.
